output.narrative_summary: This result rests on the link from Query Load Growth to Platform Cost. If query load grows faster than expected, platform cost pressure could rise in this model. In this model, 77% of runs supported Renew for One Year.

story_headlines.opt_renew: Renew for One Year holds up because projected query load growth stays within manageable cost impact in this model.

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in about 88% of variations, based on current estimates.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: Query Load Growth has the strongest modelled link to Platform Cost and is not fully evidence backed.
stability_factors: Platform Cost shows a consistent relationship with Query Load Growth across modelled runs
fragility_factors: The link from Query Load Growth to Platform Cost is the main factor with scope for change

output.readiness_rationale: This decision is settled enough to act on: the comparison holds in most variations, though Query Load Growth is not yet evidence backed and is worth firming up before committing.

fac_query_load.specific_action: Pull actual query volume trends from warehouse usage logs over the last two to three quarters.
fac_query_load.rationale: Query Load Growth has the largest influence on how platform cost unfolds under renewal.
fac_query_load.decision_hygiene: Estimate the expected query growth rate before looking at the usage logs.

key_assumptions: The link from Query Load Growth to Platform Cost assumes current usage patterns continue without major architectural change
The brief assumes a one year renewal is the only option under consideration, with no alternative contract lengths modelled

decision_quality_prompts.question: What would make you switch away from Renew for One Year?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: The comparison is well supported on current estimates, so it is worth actively checking what evidence would change that.

decision_quality_prompts.question: What is the base rate for query load growth in similar warehouse renewals?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: Confidence in Query Load Growth is not yet firmly evidence backed, so an outside view helps calibrate it.

pre_mortem.failure_scenario: Renewal looked settled but query load grew faster than modelled, pushing Platform Cost well past expectations within the contract year.
warning_signs: Query volumes rising faster month over month than historical trend
Platform cost invoices tracking above the modelled range early in the term
pre_mortem.mitigation: Set a checkpoint to review actual query load against modelled growth partway through the contract term.
pre_mortem.review_trigger: Reconvene if query load growth tracks meaningfully above modelled expectations before the next planning cycle.
